record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: For Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms on closed symplectic manifolds, if the number of periodic orbits is not finite, is the growth rate of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits at least quadratic, meaning that the lower logarithmic growth of the primitive-periodic-orbit count P(T) is at least 2?

evidence.quote: the growth of periodic orbits is at least quadratic

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold and let $\varphi\colon M\to M$ be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism, i.e. the time-one map of a smooth time-dependent Hamiltonian flow on $M$. A periodic orbit of $\varphi$ of period $k\in\mathbb{N}$ is a point $x\in M$ with $\varphi^{k}(x)=x$; it is primitive if $k$ is its minimal such period. Two periodic orbits are geometrically distinct if their underlying $\varphi$-orbits in $M$ are disjoint. For $T\geq 1$, let
$$P(T) \;=\; \#\bigl\{\text{geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits of }\varphi\text{ with period }\leq T\bigr\},$$
and define the lower logarithmic growth rate
$$\underline{\gamma}(\varphi) \;=\; \liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\log P(T)}{\log T}.$$
Question: Suppose that $\varphi$ has infinitely many geometrically distinct periodic orbits. Is it always true that
$$\underline{\gamma}(\varphi) \;\geq\; 2,$$
that is, that the number of geometrically distinct primitive periodic orbits of $\varphi$ grows at least quadratically in the period?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of growth rates of primitive periodic orbits for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms is a well-known open direction beyond the Conley conjecture. Generic results yield only sub-linear growth (e.g., k/log k for primes), and more recent work (such as growth bounds via Floer barcodes) addresses related but distinct quantitative versions. No source confirms a proof or disproof of an unconditional quadratic lower bound on $P(T)$ for general Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms with infinitely many periodic orbits, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Conley Conjecture and Beyond
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the Conley conjecture and quantitative refinements about the number of periodic orbits of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative growth refinements of the Conley conjecture remain an active research area without a proven general quadratic lower bound.

status_evidence.title: On the Growth of the Floer Barcode
status_evidence.snippet: Studies growth of Floer-theoretic invariants and periodic orbit counts for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Growth-rate questions for periodic orbits of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms are actively studied and not settled in the quadratic generality.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolic Fixed Points and Periodic Orbits of Hamiltonian Diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Existence results for infinitely many periodic orbits under hyperbolicity hypotheses; generic growth like k/log k is mentioned.
status_evidence.claim: Known generic lower bounds on primitive periodic orbit counts are sub-linear, far below quadratic.
